## What the docs say that the brief MISSED — TRANSMIT vs RECEIVE (critical)

The brief is written almost entirely in the **receive** direction ("note map," "CC map," "bank select to *reach* sounds"). The documentation is explicit that the EP-40 Riddim is **bidirectional — it TRANSMITS note and MIDI data when its own pads/controls are played, not only receives.** This is the single most important omission.

Verbatim evidence (from `/guides/ep-40/modes`, MIDI section):

> "the (knobX) knob controls the MIDI channel the pad **receives and sends to**. this allows you to connect a series of external music devices and **send note data to them all individually from different pads**!"

> "for more information on how to configure midi, as well as what midi messages are **sent and recieved**, please see the midi chart."

And from `/guides/ep-40/system`:

- The MIDI implementation chart has **two columns — "Transmitted" and "Recognised"** — not a receive-only chart. The note ranges (36-83 across groups a–d, Keys 0-127) populate **both** columns.
- Default channel behaviour is **"Receive all channels, send on MIDI channel 1"** — i.e. OMNI-in, but it *does send* on channel 1.

**Conclusion for the capability doc:** State plainly that touching a pad/knob **outputs** MIDI (note on, and per-pad channel/CC) to external gear, in addition to responding to incoming MIDI. Per the chart, transmit+receive coverage extends to **Program Change, System Exclusive, Song Position, Song Select, Tune Request, Clock, and system-real-time Commands** — so the device can act as a **MIDI controller and a clock master (SYNC/Clock Out), not just a slave.** A per-pad MIDI-channel assignment (via knobX) is the notable transmit feature to call out: different pads can drive different external instruments on different channels.

Caveat to keep the doc honest: the literal `o`/`x` transmit/receive glyphs in TE's implementation chart did not survive text extraction cleanly (they came through as `x`/`-`, which contradicts TE's own "send note data" prose). The transmit conclusion above rests on the **verbatim prose and the two-column chart structure**, which are unambiguous; do not quote individual chart `o`/`x` cells as authoritative without re-checking them on-device or against the PDF.

## Other items in the docs worth capturing (beyond the brief's list)

- **Pitch Bend** is supported (listed in the implementation chart) — the brief's CC list omits it.
- **SYNC / clock master:** 1.0.5 changed SYNC OUT to a **continuous clock**; combined with Clock-Out mode (code 102), the device can master external tempo.
- **Full mode set:** Mode 1–4 (OMNI ON/OFF × POLY/MONO) are all listed; the brief only names Mode 1.
- **Version history depth:** 2.5.1 (2026.07.03) also fixes *"note-on velocity did not work for samples"* and *"GROUP+PAD shortcut broken in TEMPO"* — relevant if the doc discusses velocity behaviour.
